summary: Full linked-list teardown: sets a dirty flag, walks every node via the next pointer, frees each node's inner data (string buffer then struct) when the per-node byte flag is set, frees the node frame itself, then zeroes head, tail, cursor and count. Returns 0.

operations.description: Set the byte at this+0x6D0 to 1 before tearing down the list.
Load the head pointer from this+0x6C0 into the traversal cursor.
While the traversal cursor is non-null, capture the current node, save the byte flag at node+0xC, advance the cursor through the next pointer at node+0x4, and process the captured node.
When the node's byte flag at +0xC is non-zero, read the inner data pointer from node+0x0 and free it.
If the inner data pointer is non-null, free the string stored at +0x4 inside it and then free the inner struct itself.
Free the node frame that was just walked.
Reset the list state to empty: zero head at this+0x6C0, tail at this+0x6C4, cursor at this+0x6C8 and count at this+0x6CC.
